name: Gaza functional area
limitations: All 31 subpillars are reviewed, not all measured. Four dimensions have conditional judgments; four remain unresolved, with no total centre or redistributed weights. Strip-level evidence is not a Gaza municipality measurement or a resolved FUA population join. No ranking or exclusion bound. Rejecting necessary assumptions leaves their dimensions unresolved.

dimensions.rationale: Identified flood and winter-shelter exposure has important protection constraints; drainage repair and voluntary relocation are operating but materials, land and funding remain inadequate.
dimensions.assumption: Documented weather exposure and inadequate protection materially affect this FUA and persist to the cutoff. Strip-wide counts are not FUA measurements; inconsistent headline and body counts are not used. Conflict itself is not a natural hazard.

dimensions.rationale: Lower conflict intensity after the ceasefire is retained as mitigation, but current repeated civilian harm and displacement indicate serious protection failure.
dimensions.assumption: Documented major civilian impacts apply to this FUA and persist to the cutoff. Historical event counts are research-priority signals, not current rates; recovered remains and revised totals are not new weekly killings.

dimensions.rationale: Response and adaptation activities are observed, but governance, social cohesion and recovery effectiveness are not sufficiently resolved across responsible actors and resident groups.
dimensions.assumption: No whole-dimension tier is assumed. War, national context and missing evidence do not establish governance or resilience failure.

dimensions.rationale: Current essential water and energy shortfalls and constrained logistics support severe basic-supply failure; aid, water trucking and improved food and cargo entry remain positive counterevidence.
dimensions.assumption: Severe basic-supply constraints materially affect ordinary residents in this FUA and persist to the cutoff despite alternatives. Aid dependence alone is not penalized; 2025 famine and projected deterioration are not current observations.

dimensions.rationale: Partially operating hospitals, consultations and evacuations coexist with severe unmet essential cancer, dialysis, diagnostic and rehabilitation needs and fragile system continuity.
dimensions.assumption: Severe necessary-care barriers broadly apply to this FUA and remain inadequately mitigated at the cutoff. Partial operation is neither zero care nor normal necessary-care access; consultation counts do not measure clinical outcomes.

dimensions.rationale: No sufficiently verified local human-evidence, regulatory-adoption and ordinary-resident access pathway supports a whole-dimension tier.
dimensions.assumption: No tier is assumed. Missing studies, war or MED failure do not establish absent longevity capability.

dimensions.rationale: Network sample absence and incomplete research-site and diffusion assessment do not support a technology-capability tier.
dimensions.assumption: No tier is assumed. Zero samples do not imply zero connectivity, knowledge production or resident adoption.

dimensions.rationale: Actual medical evacuation is verified but does not resolve general resident travel, relocation, financial or communication paths.
dimensions.assumption: No whole-dimension tier is assumed from special patient pathways, airport flags or inaccessible procedural pages; ordinary-resident permissions and alternatives require verification.
